books.section: Topic 1.3 European Exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Christopher Columbus, Journal of the First Voyage, 12 October 1492, as copied by Bartolome de las Casas, public domain

parts.modelAnswer: Columbus saw the Taíno as gentle, unarmed people who would make fine servants. He believed a small force of fifty men could subjugate them all.
parts.prompt: Identify Columbus's attitude toward the Taíno people he met.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for identifying Columbus's attitude, such as seeing the Taíno as submissive, unarmed, or fit to serve.
scoring.notEarned: Describing the Taíno without stating Columbus's attitude toward them does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The passage shows that from the first landing, the Spanish aimed to rule Native peoples and put them to work. Columbus judged the Taíno by their usefulness as subjects and servants, not as equals.
parts.prompt: Explain what the passage shows about Spanish aims in the Americas.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate Spanish aim shown in the passage, such as subjugation, rule, or forced labor.
scoring.notEarned: Restating Columbus's words without explaining what they show about Spanish aims does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The entry survives only in a copy made by Las Casas decades later, so the words may not be exactly Columbus's. Columbus was also writing to justify his voyage to the crown, so he had reason to stress how easily the new lands could be ruled.
parts.prompt: Explain one limitation of this journal entry as evidence about the voyage.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate limitation, such as the Las Casas copy, the time gap, or Columbus writing to justify himself to the crown.
scoring.notEarned: Naming Las Casas without explaining why the copy limits the entry does not earn the point.

stimulus.source_note: Christopher Columbus, Journal of the First Voyage, 12 October 1492, as copied by Bartolome de las Casas (public domain). Verbatim short excerpt from the commonly used translation.
stimulus.text: They do not bear arms, and do not know them, for I showed them a sword, they took it by the edge and cut themselves out of ignorance. They have no iron. Their spears are made of cane. They would make fine servants. With fifty men we could subjugate them all and make them do whatever we want.
